sara (runtime): Heads-up: in the soak run last night we saw a reproducible p99 latency spike around the 1024->1050 token boundary on H100 pools. Quick profile pasted below.

miguel (perf): Can you paste the profile snippet? Is it only H100 or A100 too?

sara (runtime): Paste:
```
[profile] seq=1000..1030 path=decode KERNEL=matmul_fused variant=v2 latency_p50=9.8ms p95=28.2ms p99=46.1ms
[profile] seq=980..1000 path=prefill KERNEL=matmul_split variant=v1 latency_p50=6.1ms p95=12.6ms p99=14.8ms
[profile] kvcache_evictions=0->127 window=30s
[profile] memcpy_gpu2cpu spikes coincident at seq~=1024
```

priya (infra): I checked infra metrics: eviction_count + memcpy rate both jump when the path flips. Looks like path switch triggers a cache handoff and an unexpected layout change.

kyle (prod): Our autotuner currently chooses path based on average sequence length in the sampling window. If the distribution is bimodal (short+very long), the mean can sit near the threshold and we oscillate. Do we have hysteresis?

miguel (perf): Not enough. Also suspected kernel mismatch on H100: the v2 fused kernel assumes a different tile layout and ends up forcing an expensive reorder + extra memcpy during KV handoff. A100 is more forgiving, H100 kernel is faster but brittle.

sara (runtime): Repro locally with a bimodal input mix. When we switch from prefill->decode at 1024, we see:
``
[0] prefill path: KERNEL=matmul_split layout=rowmajor
[1] decode path: KERNEL=matmul_fused layout=colmajor
action: runtime re-layout -> memcpy GPU->CPU->GPU (cost ~18-24ms for batch size 8 on H100)
```

ops-qa: That explains p99 spikes. Any quick mitigation we can canary?

kyle (prod): Short term: 1) change autotune to use p95 sequence length rather than mean, 2) add 2-step hysteresis around the threshold (+/- 64 tokens), 3) prefer kernel variants that keep layout consistent across prefill/decode handoff.

priya (infra): We can schedule a canary on a subset of H100 racks tomorrow morning at 06:00 UTC. Need PR for autotune change + runtime toggle.

miguel (perf): Also propose we tweak autotune windowing: prefer percentile-based pick and add a penalty term for kernel_layout_flip to avoid expensive handoffs.

kyle (prod): I'll open the quick PR for hysteresis + p95 picking, will flag the kernel_layout_flip as a separate follow-up to avoid blocking rollout. PR: https://internal/redwood/pulls/3289 (draft).

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/h100/06:00 UTC -> 10% traffic, rollback on p95 increase > 10% or error rate > 0.5% :rotating_light:

sara (runtime): I'll add perf traces and KV cache histograms to the canary dashboards. Will also attach flamegraphs from the next run.

ops-qa: Please add a short reproducer script and a Minimal Load test to the job so we can catch this in CI.

kyle (prod): will do the reproducer in the PR. Quick note: prefer not to change kernel selection default; we'll gate behind runtime toggle until we validate.

miguel (perf): Hypothesis summary: path boundary + bimodal seqlen -> autotune picks unstable threshold -> on flip runtime selects layout-incompatible kernel -> KV handoff triggers re-layout + memcpy -> p99 spike on H100. Fix path: p95-based threshold + hysteresis + layout-aware kernel preference.

sara (runtime): Sounds good. I'll run local soak with the new autotune logic once PR lands. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
